definitions.explanation: The evening or night immediately preceding a particular day or event.

examples.japanese: {試験|しけん}の{前夜|ぜんや}は{緊張|きんちょう}した。
examples.english: I was nervous the night before the exam.

examples.japanese: クリスマスの{前夜|ぜんや}にプレゼントを{用意|ようい}した。
examples.english: I prepared presents on Christmas Eve.

examples.japanese: {革命|かくめい}{前夜|ぜんや}のような{緊迫|きんぱく}した{空気|くうき}が{街|まち}に{漂|ただよ}っていた。
examples.english: A tense atmosphere, like the eve of a revolution, hung over the city.

notes:
Can be used literally for the night before an event, or figuratively to describe the period just before a major change or upheaval (e.g., {革命|かくめい}{前夜|ぜんや}, the eve of revolution).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{前夜|ぜんや}{祭|さい} (eve festival, the night-before celebration)
・{試合|しあい}の{前夜|ぜんや} (the night before the match)
・{開幕|かいまく}{前夜|ぜんや} (the eve of the opening)
